assumptions: finArea_m2=0.015: total pectoral lifting area, wing loading ~49 N/m2, plausible for a 0.25 m flying fish.
CLmax=1.2: moderate maximum lift coefficient for a fish fin wing.
airspeed_m_s=10: above stall speed (~8.2 m/s from W=0.736 N, S, CLmax), so required CL ≈ 0.80 < CLmax.
LD_max=8: glide ratio; bounds glide distance from 1 m at 8 m.
powered=false: added explicitly alongside flight_mode glide so C14/E3 are out of scope.
notes: I ran no check, so I haven't confirmed any verdicts. By hand, the numbers are consistent: airspeed is above stall speed, glide distance is within LD_max times the launch height, and the drag terms agree. A real flying fish glides much farther than 5 m, but that relies on powered taxiing and wind or wave lift, which this unpowered 1 m launch excludes. C14 and E3 are out of scope because the glide is unpowered. I don't know of any law that blocks this brief.
